source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: In the days of Herod, king of Judah, [there was] a certain priest whose name was Zechariah, from the priestly division [or: lineage] of Abijah, and his wife was from the daughters [or: descendants] of Aaron, and her name was Elisheva.

translation_notes: מלך (M-L-K): Candidates: H4427 'to reign', H4428 'a king', H4429 'Melek (name)', H4430 'a king (Aramaic)', H4431 'advice', H4432 'Molek'. Chose H4428 because the word is in apposition to a proper noun (Herodas) and describes his role as king of Yehudah.
כהן (K-H-N): Candidates: H3547 'to officiate as priest', H3548 'a priest', H3549 'a priest (Aramaic)'. Chose H3548 because the context describes a person ('one priest') not an action.
אחד (A-Ch-D): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because it modifies כהן as 'a certain priest.'
מבני: The prefix מ (from) + בני (sons of). Not the proper name Mebunnai (H4012), since the context describes lineage from Aaron.
ושמה: The prefix ו (and) + שמה parsed as 'her name' (שם + ה possessive suffix). Not H8047 'ruin' or H8048 'Shammah', since the context introduces a woman's name.
textual_notes: מיחס is not found in the Strong's lexicon as a single entry; it appears to be מ (from) + יחס (genealogy/division), referring to the priestly course. This is a post-biblical Hebrew term for lineage/division.

verses.literal: In [the] days of Herodas king [of] Yehudah [there was] a priest one his name Zechariah from [the] division of Aviyah and his wife was from [the] sons of Aharon and her name Elisheva

verses.translation: And both of them were righteous before God, walking [or: standing firm] in the commandments and in the righteous [requirements] of YHWH, without any blemish [or: slander, reproach].

translation_notes: האל (H-A-L): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because with the definite article ה it reads 'the God,' fitting the context of being righteous before God.

במצות: The only Strong's candidate given is H4695 'a quarrel,' but the consonants מצות clearly correspond to the plural of מצוה (commandment, H4687). The provided candidate H4695 does not fit; the context of walking in God's requirements demands 'commandments.' I assign this to the common Hebrew noun מצוות (commandments), related to H4687.
ובצדק (Ts-D-Q): Candidates: H6663 'to be right', H6664 'the right/equity'. Chose H6664 because the preposition ב + noun 'righteousness' fits the parallel structure with במצות.
שום (SH-W-M): Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7762 'garlic'. Chose H7760 in its sense of 'any/placing' — here functioning as 'any' in the phrase 'without any slander.'
textual_notes: במצות: The Strong's candidate provided (H4695 'quarrel') does not match the context. The consonants are identical to the plural of מצוה (commandment), which is the standard reading. No Strong's number for מצוה was provided in the candidates.
עומדים could mean 'standing' or 'persisting/walking firmly.' In context it suggests steadfast adherence to commandments.
בזולת is a compound preposition (without/apart from) not broken down in Strong's; it functions as 'without.'

verses.literal: And they were both of them righteous before the God walking in [the] commandments and in [the] righteousness of YHWH without any slander

verses.translation: And they had no son or daughter, because she was barren, and both of them were very advanced in age.

translation_notes: היה (H-Y-H): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because the sentence describes a state of being — they had no child.
בן (B-N): Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'a son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 because the context is about offspring.
בת (B-T): Candidates: H1323 'a daughter', H1324 'a bath (measure)', H1325 same. Chose H1323 because paired with בן (son) in a statement about children.
כי (K-Y): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: because/that'. Chose H3588 because it introduces a causal clause.
מאד (M-A-D): Candidates: H3966 'vehemently/very', H108 'fog'. Chose H3966 because it intensifies 'old.'

verses.literal: And not was to them a son or a daughter because she was barren and both of them were very old

verses.translation: It happened that when Zechariah the priest was carrying out [his] priestly duties before YHWH, in the order [or: appointed sequence] of his division's turn,

translation_notes: קרה (Q-R-H): Candidates: H7135 'coolness', H7136 'to light upon/happen', H7137 'an occurrence'. Chose H7136 because it introduces a narrative event ('it came to pass').
כאשר: Prefix כ + אשר. Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', etc. Chose H834 because כאשר is the standard temporal conjunction 'when/as.'
הכהן (H-K-H-N): Candidates: H3547 'to officiate', H3548 'a priest', H3549 'priest (Aramaic)'. Chose H3548 with definite article — 'the priest.'
פעם (P-'-M): Candidates: H6470 'to tap/beat', H6471 'a stroke/time/turn'. Chose H6471 because it means 'turn/time,' referring to the rotation of priestly service.
textual_notes: מאומנות has no Strong's candidate provided. It appears to derive from אמונה/אומנות meaning 'craft, service, faithfulness' — here referring to priestly duties/office.
בשבתו could be parsed as ב + שבת + ו (in his sitting/dwelling/division). The context of priestly rotation suggests 'his division's [scheduled service].'

verses.literal: It came to pass that as Zechariah the priest was conducting [the] service before YHWH in [the] order of [the] turn of his division

verses.translation: According to the custom of the priests, he was chosen by lot to offer [or: burn] frankincense, and as he entered into the sanctuary [or: holy place] of YHWH,

translation_notes: מנהג (M-N-H-G): Candidates: H4491 'the driving of a chariot', H5090 'to drive/lead'. Chose H4491 as the noun, but in context it means 'custom/practice' — the word's semantic range extends to any manner of conducting oneself, not just chariot-driving.
לבונה (L-B-W-N-H): Candidates: H3828 'frankincense', H3829 'Lebonah (place)', H946 'Bunah (name)'. Chose H3828 because the context describes offering incense in the sanctuary.
וכאשר: ו + כ + אשר. Chose H834 for אשר — temporal conjunction 'and when.'
במקדש (B-M-Q-D-SH): Candidates: H4720 'a sanctuary/consecrated place', H6942 'to be clean', H6944 'a sacred place'. Chose H4720 because the prefix ב + noun 'sanctuary' fits entering a holy place.
textual_notes: יצא בגורל: 'he went out by lot' — the verb יצא literally means 'went out/came forth,' but in context with בגורל it means 'his lot came out' or 'he was chosen by lot.'
שיתן is a relative particle ש + יתן (he would give/offer), not in Strong's as a unit. The verb is נתן (H5414, to give).
נכנס is not in the classical Strong's lexicon; it derives from the root כנס (to gather/enter, post-biblical usage for 'to enter').

verses.literal: According to [the] custom of the priests he went out by lot that he would give frankincense and as he entered into [the] sanctuary of YHWH

verses.translation: And all the people were outside, praying at the hour [or: moment] when it was [appointed] for him to offer the frankincense.

translation_notes: העם ('-M): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5971 because with the definite article it reads 'the people,' the subject of the sentence.
בשעה (SH-'-H): Candidates: H8159 'to gaze/inspect', H8160 'a look/moment'. Chose H8160 because with ב it reads 'at the moment/hour,' a temporal marker.
שהיה: ש (relative particle) + היה. H1961 'to exist/be' fits — 'that it was [time] for him.'
הלבונה: ה (the) + לבונה. Candidates: H3828 'frankincense', H3829 'Lebonah (place)'. Chose H3828, same reasoning as section 5.

verses.literal: And all the people were outside praying at [the] hour that it was for him to give the frankincense

verses.translation: But a messenger [or: angel] of YHWH, standing at the right side of the altar of frankincense, appeared to him.

translation_notes: אבל (A-B-L): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'truly/yet/but'. Chose H61 because it functions as an adversative conjunction 'but/yet,' introducing a surprising new element in the narrative.
מלאך (M-L-A-K): Candidates: H4397 'a messenger/angel', H4398 'an angel (Aramaic)'. Chose H4397 because this is a Hebrew text and the word introduces a divine messenger.
ימין (Y-M-Y-N): Candidates: H3225 'the right hand/side', H3226 'Jamin (name)'. Chose H3225 because it describes the spatial position beside the altar.
הלבונה: H3828 'frankincense' — the altar of frankincense, the incense altar.
textual_notes: עומד could be a participle (standing) modifying מלאך, or the beginning of a new clause. The participial reading is more natural: 'a messenger standing at the right side.'

verses.literal: But a messenger of YHWH standing at [the] side [of the] right of the altar of the frankincense appeared to him

verses.translation: And when Zechariah saw him, he was terrified [or: alarmed], and fear [or: awe, dread] fell upon him.

translation_notes: וכאשר: ו + כ + אשר. Chose H834 — temporal conjunction 'and when.'
היה (H-Y-H): Candidates: H1961 'to be/become', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 as the auxiliary verb with נבהל.

ובאה: Candidates: H872 'an entrance'. However, in context this reads as ו + באה, the verb בוא (to come, H935) in 3fs perfect form — 'and [fear] came.' The candidate H872 does not fit the syntax. I read this as a form of בוא.
יראה (Y-R-A-H): H3374 'fear/reverence'. Fits perfectly as the subject of the verb באה — 'fear came upon him.'
textual_notes: ובאה: The provided candidate H872 ('entrance') does not fit the syntax. The consonants match the 3fs perfect of בוא (to come), with יראה (feminine noun) as its subject. This is the more coherent reading.
זכריהו is a variant spelling of זכריה (Zechariah) with the longer theophoric suffix -הו.

verses.literal: And as Zechariah saw him he was terrified and fear came upon him

verses.translation: But the messenger [or: angel] said to him: Do not fear, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard, and your wife Elisheva will bear you a son, and you shall call his name Yochanan [meaning: YHWH is gracious].

translation_notes: אבל (A-B-L): Same as section 7 — chose H61 'but/yet' as adversative conjunction, transitioning from Zechariah's fear to the angel's reassurance.
אל (A-L): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'God', H413 'to/near'. Chose H408 because אל + תירא is the standard prohibitive construction 'do not fear.'

אומר: The candidate given is H201 'Omar (name)'. However, the consonants א-מ-ר are clearly the participle of אמר (to say, H559). The Strong's candidate list is incomplete; this is the verb 'says/is saying.'
בן (B-N): Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'a son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 — the angel announces the birth of a son.
textual_notes: אומר: The only Strong's candidate provided (H201 'Omar') is a proper name and does not fit. The consonants are identical to the active participle of אמר (H559, to say). I treat this as the verb 'says.'
א0לישבע: The 0 appears to be a scribal mark or damage in the manuscript. The consonants otherwise match אלישבע (H472, Elisheva).

verses.literal: But the messenger says to him do not fear Zechariah because your prayer has been heard and your wife Elisheva will bear to you a son and you will call his name Yochanan

verses.translation: And there will be joy and exultation [or: gladness] for you, and many will rejoice when he is born.

translation_notes: שמחה (S-M-Ch-H): Candidates: H8057 'blithesomeness/glee', H4229 'to stroke/erase'. Chose H8057 because the context is about celebration at the announcement of a birth.
וגיל (G-Y-L): Candidates: H1523 'to spin round/rejoice', H1524 'joy/an age'. Chose H1524 as the noun 'gladness/joy,' paired with שמחה in a hendiadys of joyful celebration.
textual_notes: כשיהיה is a compound: כ (when) + ש (relative) + יהיה (he will be). This is a later Hebrew construction. Combined with נולד (passive participle of ילד, 'born'), it reads 'when he is born.'

verses.literal: And there will be joy and gladness to you and many will rejoice when he is born

verses.translation: For he will be great before the Mighty One [or: God], and he will not drink wine or intoxicating drink [or: strong drink]. Before he comes forth from the womb of his mother, he will be filled to completion [or: made whole, perfected] by the spirit of holiness [or: the holy spirit].

translation_notes: האל (consonants אל with article ה): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because 'great before the God' makes contextual sense—describing status before a deity.

ושכר (consonants שכר with ו): Candidates: H7936 'to hire', H7937 'to become tipsy', H7941 'intoxicating liquor', H7938/H7939 'wages'. Chose H7941 because paired with 'wine' it forms the classic pair wine-and-strong-drink, a Nazirite-type prohibition.

מרוח (consonants מ + רוח): Candidates: H4790 'bruised/emasculated', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit'. Chose H7307 because 'filled from the spirit of holiness' fits the context of a child set apart from the womb; H4790 makes no sense here.

הקדש (consonants קדש with article ה): Candidates: H6942 'to make clean', H6944 'sacred place/thing/sanctity', H6945 'devotee'. Chose H6944 because 'the holiness' or 'the sanctity' naturally pairs with 'spirit' to form 'the spirit of holiness.'
נשלם: Parsed as nifal passive/reflexive of שלם (H7999 'to be complete/safe'). The nifal yields 'be completed/made whole/perfected,' fitting the context of being filled with the spirit.
textual_notes: קודם is not in the provided Strong's candidates—it appears to be a later Hebrew/Aramaic adverb meaning 'before/prior to.' No Strong's number assigned.
נשלם could be parsed as nifal perfect or nifal participle of שלם. Both yield 'completed/perfected' but the temporal sense differs slightly (will be completed vs. being completed).

verses.literal: For he will be great before the God and not will he drink wine and strong drink before that he goes out from [the] womb [of] his mother he will be completed from [the] spirit [of] the holiness

verses.translation: And he will go [or: be established] before him—that is, before YHWH—in the spirit and in the power [or: vigor] of Elijah, in order that he may turn [or: settle, restore] the heart of the fathers toward the children, and guide them in the wisdom of the righteous, and prepare for YHWH a people made whole [or: complete, at peace].
words: that he will cause to return/settle

translation_notes: ויבונן: Could be hitpolel of בין (H995 'to understand/discern') or possibly a form suggesting 'to go/establish oneself.' In context 'he will go before him' fits the messenger-forerunner role. The hitpolel of בין can mean 'to show oneself discerning' or 'to present oneself.' Chose H995 broadly as 'he will present himself/go.'
זהו: Demonstrative pronoun זה (H2088) with 3ms pronominal suffix or copular usage—'that is he' / 'that is.' Functions as an explanatory gloss: 'before him, that is, before YHWH.'

אליהו (consonants אליהו): H453 is listed as 'Elihu,' but these exact consonants also spell 'Eliyahu' (Elijah). The context of spirit and power of a prophetic forerunner matches Elijah. The Strong's entry H453 covers this name form.

שישב (ש + ישב): H3427 'to sit/dwell/return.' In hifil causative 'to cause to sit/settle/return'—'to turn/restore the heart of the fathers toward the sons.' This fits the forerunner-reconciliation theme.
בבנים: H1143 'space between armies' doesn't fit. More naturally בנים = plural of בן (H1121 'son'). With prefix ב = 'in/among the sons.'

ויכין: H3199 is 'Jakin' (proper name). But the consonants also parse as ו + יכין from כון (H3559 'to establish/prepare') in hifil imperfect. Chose H3559 because 'he will prepare for YHWH a people' is coherent; a proper name makes no sense here.
עם: Candidates H5971 'people' vs H5973 'with.' Chose H5971 because 'prepare for YHWH a people complete' is coherent.
שלם: Candidates include H8003 'complete/whole/friendly,' H8004 'Shalem (Jerusalem),' H7999 'to be complete.' Chose H8003 as adjective 'complete' modifying 'people.'
textual_notes: ויבונן is morphologically ambiguous—it could be hitpolel of בין or possibly a polel form. The translation 'go/present himself' is contextual.
אליהו: H453 is labeled 'Elihu' in Strong's but the consonants are identical to Elijah (אליהו). Context strongly indicates the prophet Elijah.
שישב in hifil could mean 'cause to sit/dwell' or 'cause to return/restore.' Both are plausible; 'turn/restore the heart' is the more natural image for reconciliation.

verses.literal: And he will go before him that is before YHWH in [the] spirit and in [the] power [of] Eliyahu in order that he will cause to dwell [the] heart [of] the fathers in [the] sons and he will guide them in [the] wisdom [of] the righteous and he will prepare for YHWH a people complete

verses.translation: And Zechariah said to the messenger [or: angel], How will this be done? For I am old, and my wife is advanced in her days.

translation_notes: ואמר: Candidates include H559 'to say,' H561 'something said,' H563 'a lamb.' Chose H559 as the verb 'said' fits the narrative context of dialogue.
למלאך: H4397 'messenger/angel' vs H4398 'angel' (Aramaic). Chose H4397 as the Hebrew form.
זה: H2088 'this/that' vs H2089 'a sheep.' Chose H2088—'how will this be done' is coherent; 'how will a sheep be done' is not.
זקן: H2204 'to be old,' H2205 'old (adj),' H2206 'beard.' Chose H2205 as predicate adjective: 'I am old.'

מהרה ימיה: H4120 'hurry/promptly' + 'her days.' This could mean 'advanced/far along in her days.' Alternatively מ + הרה (H2029/H2030 'pregnant/to conceive') would yield 'from pregnancy her days'—which doesn't fit since she hasn't yet conceived. Chose H4120: 'hurried/advanced in her days' = she is elderly.
textual_notes: מהרה could be parsed as מ + הרה (H2029 'to conceive/be pregnant'), but contextually Zechariah is explaining why conception seems impossible, not stating she is pregnant. H4120 'hurried/advanced' better fits the complaint about old age.
ואשתי is not in the provided candidates—parsed as וְ + אשת + י (my wife), from אשה (H802).

verses.literal: And said Zechariah to the messenger how will be done this that I [am] old and my wife [is] advanced [in] her days

verses.translation: And the messenger [or: angel] answered and said to him, I am the one who stands before the Mighty One [or: God], and I have been sent to announce [or: declare, make known] to you these words.

translation_notes: וענה: H6030 'to respond/answer' vs H6031 'to depress/afflict.' Chose H6030—'the messenger answered' fits dialogue context.
הוא: H1931 'he/self' vs H1933 'to be.' Chose H1931—'I am he' = 'I am the one' (emphatic self-identification).
האל: H410 'God/mighty' vs H408 'not.' Chose H410—'stands before God' is coherent for an angelic messenger.
להגיד: The provided candidate H1517 'a thong/tendon' for גיד doesn't fit. The consonants ה-ג-י-ד parse as hifil infinitive of נגד (H5046 'to declare/announce'). Chose H5046.
אלה: Candidates H421-H426. These consonants also match H428 (אלה 'these'). Chose H428 as demonstrative pronoun 'these'—'these words' is natural.
ושולחתי: Parsed as passive/pual participle or nifal of שלח (H7971 'to send') + 1cs suffix: 'I have been sent.' Alternatively active: 'I was sent.'
שעומד: ש (relative 'who') + עומד (participle of עמד H5975 'to stand'): 'who stands.'
textual_notes: אלה consonants match both H428 'these' (demonstrative) and H426 'God' (Aramaic). Context clearly demands 'these' as it modifies 'the words.'
להגיד: The Strong's candidate provided (H1517 'tendon') does not match. This is clearly הגיד = hifil infinitive construct of נגד (H5046), a common verb meaning 'to tell/declare.'

verses.literal: And answered the messenger and said to him I [am] he who stands before the God and I have been sent to declare to you these the words

verses.translation: Because you did not believe [or: trust] my words, which will be fulfilled [or: completed] in their appointed time, you will be mute [or: speechless] and unable to speak until that day when these words come to their completion [or: fulfillment, end].

translation_notes: הא־מנת: Root אמן (H539 'to believe/trust'). The hifil 2ms perfect form הֶאֱמַנְתָּ = 'you believed.' The hyphen in the manuscript may indicate a scribal break.
לדברי: H1704 'Dibri' (proper name) doesn't fit. Parse as ל + דברי = 'to/in my words' from דבר (H1697). The yod is 1cs possessive suffix.
שיושלמו: ש (relative) + יושלמו (pual imperfect 3mp of שלם H7999): 'that will be completed/fulfilled.'
בעתן: ב + עת (H6256 'time') + ן (3fp suffix): 'in their time'—referring to the words' appointed time of fulfillment.
עד: H5704 'until' vs H5707 'witness.' Chose H5704—'until that day' is a natural temporal clause.
שאלו: ש (relative 'that') + אלו. H431 'lo!' or H432 'if.' But in context this likely = ש + אלה (these, H428) with variant spelling. 'That these words will come to completion' is coherent.
דבר: H1696 'to speak' vs H1697 'a word.' After תוכל ('you will be able'), an infinitive 'to speak' (H1696) fits.
textual_notes: שאלו: The consonants could parse as ש + אלו (H431 'lo!' or H432 'if'), or as a variant of ש + אלה ('these'). Context demands 'these' as it introduces 'these words will come to completion.'
בעתן: The feminine plural suffix ן suggests the antecedent is 'words' (דברים), which in Hebrew can take feminine reference. 'In their time' = at the appointed time for these words.

verses.literal: On account of that not you believed in my words that will be completed in their time you will be mute and not you will be able [to] speak until that day that these the words will come to completion

verses.translation: And the people were there, waiting for Zechariah, and wondering [or: marveling] why he was delayed, standing in the sanctuary [or: holy place].

translation_notes: והעם: H5971 'people' vs H5973 'with.' The article ה confirms a noun: 'the people.' Chose H5971.
היה: H1961 'to be/was' vs H1962 'ruin.' Chose H1961—'the people was there' is coherent.
שם: H8033 'there' vs H8034 'name.' Chose H8033—'was there waiting' makes sense spatially.
במקדש: H4720 'sanctuary/consecrated place' vs H6944 'sacred thing.' Chose H4720 as the noun 'sanctuary' with prefix ב.
ממתין: No Strong's candidate provided. This is a participial form meaning 'waiting' (common in later Hebrew, from root מתן/המתין).
ומתמיהים: No Strong's entry provided directly. Root תמה (H8539 'to wonder/be amazed') in hitpael participle: 'wondering/marveling.'
מתעכב: No Strong's candidate provided. Later Hebrew root עכב meaning 'to delay/be detained.' Participial form: 'delaying/being detained.'
textual_notes: ממתין, ומתמיהים, and מתעכב are later Hebrew verbal forms not well represented in the classical Strong's lexicon. They are participial forms meaning 'waiting,' 'wondering,' and 'being delayed' respectively.

verses.literal: And the people was there waiting for Zechariah and wondering why [he] delays standing in the sanctuary

verses.translation: And when he came out from the sanctuary, he was not able to speak to them, and they recognized that he had seen a vision [or: appearance]. By signs he was showing [or: indicating] to them, and he remained mute. The holiness [was] in [the] spirit of God.

translation_notes: וכאשר: H834 'who/which/when' with כ and ו prefix. 'And when' is the natural temporal conjunction.
מן: H4480 'from/out of' vs H4478 'manna.' Chose H4480—'from the sanctuary.'
לדבר: H1696 'to speak' vs H1697 'word.' After יכול 'able,' infinitive 'to speak' fits.
שמראה: ש (relative) + מראה. H4758 'a vision/appearance' vs H4759 'a vision/mirror.' Both work; chose H4758 as 'a vision/appearance' is the more common reading for something seen.
ראה: H7200 'to see' vs H7203 'a seer/vision.' Chose H7200 as the verb—'a vision he saw.'

מראה (second occurrence): Could be H4758 'vision/appearance' again, or parsed as hifil participle of ראה (H7200) 'showing/causing to see.' Context: 'by signs showing to them'—the hifil participle 'showing' fits because he is gesturing/communicating by signs.
להם: H3859 'to burn/rankle' doesn't fit. Parse as ל + הם (H1992 'them'): 'to them.'
ועמד: H5975 'to stand' vs H5976 'to shake.' Chose H5975—'he stood/remained mute.'
אלם: H481 'to be tongue-tied,' H482 'silence,' H483 'speechless.' Chose H483 as adjective 'mute/speechless.'
textual_notes: The final clause הקדש ברוח אלוה is syntactically difficult. It could be read as: (1) a separate statement about the holy spirit of God, (2) appositional to his muteness—'mute [by] the holiness in [the] spirit of God,' or (3) a displaced phrase belonging to an adjacent clause. The most natural reading seems to be that his condition was enacted through/by the holy spirit of God.
בסימנין appears to be an Aramaic/later Hebrew plural form (סימנין 'signs'). Not in classical Strong's.

שום: Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7761 'to put (Aramaic)', H7762 'garlic'. In later Hebrew שום דבר functions as 'any thing' (lit. 'a placed thing'). Chose H7760 because in context it means 'any' modifying דבר.
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because שום דבר = 'any thing/matter'.
לפני: H3942 'anterior/before' — used as a preposition meaning 'before the face of' YHWH.
יהוה: Candidates: H3068, H3069 — both YHWH. Chose H3068 as the standard divine name.
textual_notes: אינינו is a later Hebrew form (אינננו) meaning 'there is not' or 'is not for us/him'. The suffix may be third person or first person plural — context favors impersonal 'there is not'.
איפשרי is a post-biblical Hebrew word meaning 'possible', formed from the root א-פ-ש-ר. It has no Strong's number as it is not found in biblical Hebrew. The combination בלתי איפשרי = 'impossible'.
The double negation structure (אינינו שלא יהיה בלתי איפשרי) is emphatic: literally 'there is not that it will be impossible' = 'nothing will be impossible'.

verses.literal: For no thing is not that it will be impossible before YHWH

verses.translation: And Miriam [Mary] said: Behold, here [is] the maidservant [or: handmaid, servant-woman] of YHWH [the Eternal One]. Let it be done to me according to your words.

translation_notes: הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2009 because Miriam is making a declarative statement presenting herself.
פה: Candidates: H6310 'mouth', H6311 'here/this place'. Chose H6311 because 'behold here [is] the maidservant' is the natural reading — she is presenting herself as present and available.
שפחת: The provided candidate H6354 (פחת 'a pit') does not fit. The word is שפחת, construct form of שפחה (H8198, maidservant/female servant). The ש is integral to the root שפח, not a prefix.
textual_notes: שפחת — the candidates list only provides פחת H6354 'a pit', but the actual word is the construct form of שפחה 'maidservant'. This is clearly שפחת יהוה = 'the maidservant of YHWH'.
יהיה לי עשוי could be parsed as 'let it be done to me' (jussive) or 'it will be done to me' (future). The jussive sense fits the context of willing submission.

verses.literal: And she said Miriam behold here [is] the maidservant of YHWH let it be done to me according to your words

verses.translation: And Miriam [Mary] rose up from there in those days and went [or: traveled] in haste [promptly] into the hill country, to a city of Judah.

translation_notes: מהרה: Candidates: H4120 'a hurry/promptly', H2029 'to be pregnant', H2030 'pregnant'. Chose H4120 because the context describes travel — she went quickly — not a statement about pregnancy. 'She went in haste into the hills' is coherent; 'she went pregnant into the hills' is forced here.

בעיר: Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'a city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'a watcher/angel', H5895 'a young ass'. Chose H5892 because 'to a city of Judah' is the natural geographic reference for a destination of travel.
וקמה: The candidate H7054 'stalk of grain' does not fit. This is the verb קום (H6965 'to rise/stand up') in the feminine form with vav-consecutive: 'and she rose up'.
textual_notes: מ&ם appears to be משם ('from there') with a corrupted or damaged consonant represented by &. This is the standard word for 'from there'.
בהרים — this could be 'in the mountains/hills' (plural of הר, H2022) or 'in Harim' (a place name). Context of traveling to the Judean hill country favors 'in the hills/mountains'.

verses.literal: And Miriam rose from there in those days and went in haste into the hills to a city of Judah

verses.translation: And she entered into the house [or: household] of Zechariah and she gave her a greeting of peace [shalom] to Elisheva [Elizabeth].

translation_notes: בבית: Candidates: H1004 'a house', H1005 'house (Aramaic)', H1006 'Bajith (place)', H3487 'sign of object'. Chose H1004 because 'the house of Zechariah' is the clear intended meaning — she entered a household.

שלום: Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare/greeting', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. Chose H7965 because giving שלום is the standard Hebrew greeting, meaning she greeted Elisheva with peace.
textual_notes: לאץלישבע — the form is unusual with the צ prefix. This appears to be a variant or scribal form of לאלישבע ('to Elisheva/Elizabeth'). The צ may represent a dialectal or scribal convention in this manuscript.
ונתנה לה שלום — literally 'she gave to her peace'. This is the Hebrew idiom for greeting someone, equivalent to 'she greeted her'.

verses.literal: And she entered into the house of Zechariah and she gave to her peace to Elisheva

verses.translation: And immediately when she heard the greeting [shalom] from Miriam [Mary], the child [or: boy] of Elisheva [Elizabeth] leaped with joy in her womb, and Elisheva was filled with [the] Spirit of Holiness [the Holy Spirit].

translation_notes: נער: Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy/child', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the context describes a child in the womb who responds to a greeting — 'the child of Elisheva' is the natural reading.

שמח: Candidates: H8055 'to brighten up/be glad/rejoice', H8056 'blithe/gleeful', H4220 'fat/rich', H4221 'marrow'. Chose H8055 because the child responding with joy in the womb is the coherent image — a child leaping with gladness.

מרוח: Candidates: H4790 'bruised/emasculated', H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room/interval', H7306 'to blow/smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 'spirit (Aramaic)'. Chose H7307 because 'filled from/with spirit of holiness' describes a divine infilling, consistent with the theological context.

הקדש: Candidates: H6942 'to be clean/holy', H6943 'Kedesh (place)', H6944 'a sacred place or thing/sanctity', H6945 'sacred person/devotee', H6946 'Kadesh (place)'. Chose H6944 because רוח הקדש ('spirit of the holiness') is the standard Hebrew expression for the Holy Spirit.
textual_notes: ש&מעה and ה&לום contain damaged or marked consonants (represented by &). ש&מעה is clearly ששמעה ('when she heard', with the relative ש + שמעה). ה&לום appears to be השלום ('the greeting/peace'), with the ש partially damaged.
ומיד — literally 'and from hand' but in later Hebrew this is the standard idiom for 'immediately'. The connection to H3027 (יד 'hand') is etymological; the functional meaning is 'at once'.

verses.literal: And immediately when she heard the greeting from Miriam Elisheva the child of Elisheva rejoiced in her womb and Elisheva was filled from [the] spirit of the holy

verses.translation: And she cried out [or: exclaimed] with a great [loud] voice and said: Blessed are you among the women, and blessed [is] the fruit of your womb!

translation_notes: את: Candidates: H852 'a portent', H853 'self/object marker', H854 'nearness/with', H855 'a hoe'. Chose H853 because here את functions as the second person feminine pronoun 'you' — 'blessed are you among the women'. In context this is a direct address.

בין: Candidates: H995 'to distinguish/understand', H996 'between/among', H997 'between'. Chose H996 because 'blessed you among the women' is the natural reading — comparing her status relative to other women.

וברוך: The candidate H1263 'Baruk (name)' does not fit. This is the passive participle of ברך (H1288 'to bless'), masculine form: 'and blessed [is]'. Masculine because it modifies פרי (fruit), which is masculine.
textual_notes: וצע3קה — contains a numeral 3, likely representing a damaged or uncertain consonant. The word is clearly וצעקה ('and she cried out'), from צעק (H6817). The 3 may represent a gimel or simply scribal damage.
את could be the object marker (H853) or the pronoun 'you' (feminine). In this context it functions as 'you' — the subject of the blessing.

verses.literal: And she cried out in a voice great and said blessed [are] you among the women and blessed [is the] fruit of your womb

verses.translation: And how has this come about — that the mother of my lord [or: my master] has come to me?

translation_notes: קרה: Candidates: H7135 'coolness', H7136 'to light upon/happen/come about', H7137 'an occurrence/accident'. Chose H7136 because 'how has this happened' expresses wonder at an event occurring — the arrival of the mother of her lord.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this (demonstrative)', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'this' as a demonstrative pronoun is the natural reading: 'how has this happened'.

שאם: Candidates: H517 'a mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H517 because 'that the mother of my lord has come to me' produces the coherent image of a woman expressing amazement at being visited by someone of higher status. 'If my lord' would make the clause conditional and incomplete.
באה: H872 'an entrance' as a noun, but here באה functions as the feminine perfect of בוא (H935 'to come/enter'): 'she has come'. The form is verbal, not nominal.
textual_notes: א3דוני — contains a numeral 3, likely representing a damaged consonant. The word is clearly אדוני ('my lord/my master'), from אדון (H113). The 3 may represent the letter gimel or scribal damage.

שאם — the ש prefix functions as a relative particle ('that/who') in later Hebrew, + אם 'mother'. Could theoretically be read as ש + אם 'that if', but 'that the mother' is far more coherent in context.

verses.literal: And how has this happened that the mother of my lord has come to me

verses.translation: Know [or: you should know] that when your greeting [shalom] reached my ears, the child [or: boy] leaped with great joy [or: exultation] in my womb.

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction'. Chose H3588 because this introduces a causal/explanatory clause.

הנער: Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy/child', H5289 'wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the context describes the unborn child responding to the greeting — 'the child rejoiced'.

שמח: Candidates: H8055 'to rejoice/be glad', H8056 'blithe/gleeful', H4220 'fat', H4221 'marrow'. Chose H8055 because the child rejoicing with great joy is the natural image — consistent with the preceding section's description of the child leaping.

בגיל: Candidates: H1523 'to spin round/rejoice', H1524 'joy/a revolution of time'. Chose H1524 because 'with joy' (בגיל) paired with 'great' produces 'with great joy/exultation' — a coherent description of the child's response.

אזני: The only candidate H244 is 'Ozni, an Israelite'. However, the word is clearly אזני 'my ears', from אזן (H241 'ear') with first person singular suffix. The listing of H244 is misleading — this is not a proper name here.
textual_notes: כא3שר contains a numeral 3 representing a damaged consonant — this is clearly כאשר ('when/as'), a standard temporal conjunction.
שלומך — 'your peace/greeting'. This is שלום with second person feminine suffix, referring to Miriam's greeting of peace.
שמעו אזני — literally 'my ears heard'. The subject-verb agreement (plural ears, plural verb) is standard.

verses.literal: You shall know that when your greeting heard my ears the child rejoiced with joy great in my womb

verses.translation: And blessed [or: happy] are you who believed [trusted], for indeed [or: and did not doubt, because] those words that were spoken to you from YHWH [the Eternal One] will be fulfilled [completed, brought to perfection] in you.
words: and blessed are you / happy are you

translation_notes: ולא כי: This phrase is syntactically ambiguous. Option 1: 'and [did] not [doubt], for...' — meaning she believed and did not waver, because the words will be fulfilled. Option 2: 'and not because...' which would mean her blessedness is not because of the words but for some other reason — this is incoherent in context. Chose option 1: ולא = 'and [she did] not [doubt]', כי = 'for/because' introducing the reason.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction'. Chose H3588 because this introduces the explanatory clause about why she is blessed.
יהוה: Candidates: H3068, H3069. Chose H3068 as the standard divine name.
textual_notes: שהאץמנת — this appears to be ש + האמנת ('who believed/trusted'), from אמן (H539 'to believe/trust'), with an extraneous צ possibly representing a scribal convention or dialectal spelling in this manuscript. The root is clearly אמן in the hiphil: 'she believed'.

ולא כי — the most challenging phrase in this section. It could mean: (a) 'and [she did] not [doubt], because...' (b) 'and not, for...' as a corrective statement. Option (a) produces the most coherent reading: 'blessed are you who believed and did not [doubt], for those words spoken to you from YHWH will be fulfilled in you.'
נשלמים — passive participle plural of שלם, meaning 'being completed/fulfilled/perfected'. This could also carry the sense of 'being made whole' or 'being brought to peace'.

verses.literal: And blessed are you who believed and not for those the words that were spoken to you from YHWH will be completed in you

verses.translation: And Miriam declared: My innermost being [my soul, my breath-of-life] praises and exalts [lifts up] God

translation_notes: ומעלה (מעלה/עלה): Candidates: H4608 'elevation/acclivity', H4609 'elevation/journey upward', H5927 'to ascend/mount', H5928 'holocaust', H5929 'leaf', H5930 'step/holocaust', H5931 'pretext'. Chose H5927 as a Hiphil participle (מַעֲלָה) meaning 'causes to ascend, exalts' — parallel to 'praises' and producing a coherent image of active worship.

האל (אל): Candidates: H408/H409 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411/H412 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. With the definite article ה and as the object of praise and exaltation, H410 'God' is the only coherent reading.
textual_notes: נשמתי has no Strong's candidates listed but consonants match H5397 (נְשָׁמָה) 'breath, spirit, soul' with 1cs suffix. This is the only plausible reading from the consonants.
משבחת has no candidates listed but consonants match H7623 (שׁבח) 'to praise' in a feminine participle form, agreeing with נשמתי as its subject.

verses.literal: And Miriam said my breath-of-life praises and elevates the God

verses.translation: And my spirit rejoices [is filled with gladness] in God, who is my salvation [my wholeness, my peace]

translation_notes: שמחה: Candidates: H8057 'blithesomeness/glee', H4229 (מחה) 'to stroke/erase'. In context of spirit praising God, H8057 'joy' is the coherent reading — spirit being in a state of joy.
באל: Candidates: H408/409 'not', H410 'God', H411/412 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. With prefix ב (in) and parallel to section 1's praise of God, H410 'in God' is the natural reading.
שהוא: The ש is a relative particle ('who/that'), followed by הוא. Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. H1931 as pronoun 'who he [is]' fits the relative clause structure.
textual_notes: שלומי: No candidates listed. Consonants match H7965 (שָׁלוֹם) 'peace, completeness, welfare, soundness' with 1cs suffix. Could also be parsed as the proper name Shelomi (H8015), but in context of describing God, 'my peace/salvation' is far more coherent.

verses.literal: And my spirit [is] joy in God who he [is] my wholeness

verses.translation: For he gazed upon the lowliness [the humble state] of his maidservant, and because of this all creatures will declare me to be blessed [radiant, illuminated]

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. As a conjunction opening a causal clause, H3588 is the clear reading.
הוא: H1931 'he' as the subject pronoun referring back to God from sections 1-2.

שפלות: H8220 'remissness' — but in context of a maidservant before God, the consonants שפלות more naturally read as the abstract noun from שפל (H8217) meaning 'lowliness, humble state'. H8220 is listed but its meaning 'remissness/slackness' is less fitting than the broader sense of lowliness/humility.
ובעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Causal conjunction fits perfectly here.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. H2088 as demonstrative pronoun 'this' following ובעבור forms the natural phrase 'on account of this'.
textual_notes: הבריות: No candidates listed. The consonants suggest בריות from ברא (H1254 'to create') — 'creatures/creations'. This is a post-biblical Hebrew formation but fits the consonantal text.

ה%יות: The % symbol suggests a damaged or uncertain letter. The consonants suggest היות from H1961 (היה 'to be') as an infinitive construct 'being'. The phrase אנכי היות מאורת would mean 'I am being illuminated/radiant'.

מאו(רת: The ( suggests a damaged letter. The consonants suggest מאורת from H3974 (מָאוֹר) 'luminary/light-source' or the feminine form meaning 'illuminated/blessed'. This could also relate to H835 (אשר) via a different parsing, but the consonants most naturally read as from אור 'light'. The phrase 'all creatures will call me illuminated/blessed' fits the song of praise context.
שפחתו: No candidates listed. Consonants match H8198 (שִׁפְחָה) 'maidservant/female slave' with 3ms possessive suffix — 'his maidservant'.

verses.literal: For he looked-upon [the] lowliness [of] his maidservant and on account of this all the creatures will say I [am] being illuminated

verses.translation: For the one who is wholly [entirely] able — the Holy One is his name — he has done in me [for me] great things

translation_notes: כי: H3588 as causal conjunction 'for/because'.
שהוא: ש as relative particle + הוא H1931 'he' — 'who he [is]'.
הוא: H1931 as emphatic pronoun 'he' — subject of עשה.

בי: H994 is listed as 'oh that!/with leave' but the consonants ב + י (preposition ב + 1cs suffix) simply mean 'in me/for me'. The Strong's entry H994 reflects a specific interjection use, but here it functions as the common prepositional phrase.
textual_notes: אותו: No candidates listed. Could be the direct object marker את (H853) with 3ms suffix 'him', or could be אות (H226) 'sign' with 3ms suffix 'his sign'. In context, it appears to function as a pronoun referring to God: 'for him, who is wholly able' — i.e., the direct object marker used pronominally or as emphasis.
כולו: No candidates listed. Consonants match כל (H3605) 'all/whole' with 3ms suffix — 'all of him, entirely, wholly'.
יכול: No candidates listed. Consonants match H3201 (יכל) 'to be able, to prevail' — here as an adjective/participle 'able, capable'.
שמו: No candidates listed. Consonants match H8034 (שם) 'name' with 3ms suffix — 'his name'.
דברים: No candidates listed. Consonants match H1697 (דבר) 'word, thing, matter' in masculine plural — 'things/words'.
גדולים: No candidates listed. Consonants match H1419 (גדול) 'great' in masculine plural — 'great ones/great things'.

verses.literal: For he who he [is] all-of-him able the holy-one his name he did in me things great

verses.translation: His steadfast lovingkindness [mercy, covenant-faithfulness] [endures] from generation to generation for those who revere [fear] him

translation_notes: חסד: Candidates: H2616 'to bow/be kind', H2617 'kindness/piety/lovingkindness', H2618 'Chesed (proper name)'. As a noun opening a statement about God's enduring quality, H2617 'lovingkindness' is the clear choice.

שלו: Candidates: H7958 'quail', H7959 'security', H7960 'fault', H7961 'tranquil/security'. However, in context שלו most naturally parses as the relative particle ש + ל (to/of) + ו (him) = 'that is of him / his'. This produces the coherent phrase 'His lovingkindness'. The dictionary entries treat שלו as a standalone word, but the consonants here function as a compound particle+preposition+suffix.

מדור: Candidates: H4070 'dwelling', H1752 'to remain', H1753 'to reside', H1754 'circle', H1755 'generation', H1756 'Dor (place)'. With prefix מ (from) and paired with לדור, H1755 'generation' creates the classic phrase 'from generation to generation'.
לדור: Same candidates as דור above. H1755 with prefix ל (to) completes 'from generation to generation'.
textual_notes: ליריאיו: No candidates listed. The consonants suggest ל + ירא (H3373 'fearing, one who fears') + י (plural construct) + ו (3ms suffix) = 'to those who fear him'. The י before ראי could also be parsed differently, but 'to his fearers/those who revere him' is the most natural reading.

שלו could theoretically be read as a standalone word (H7958 'quail', H7961 'tranquil') but this produces incoherent results in context. The compound reading ש+ל+ו ('that of him' = 'his') is far more natural.

verses.literal: [The] kindness of him from generation to generation to those-who-fear-him

verses.translation: For he performs mighty [powerful, forceful] deeds with his arm, and he scorns [treats with contempt] the arrogant in the scheming [imagination] of their heart

translation_notes: כי: H3588, causal conjunction.
הוא: H1931, pronoun 'he' as subject.

מבזה: Candidates: H959 'to disesteem/despise', H960 'scorned', H961 'booty', H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep'. With prefix מ as participial marker and in context of God acting against the proud, H959 'despising/scorning' in participle form produces the coherent image.
והוא: H1931 with conjunction ו, 'and he'.
textual_notes: עושה: No candidates listed. Consonants match H6213 (עשה) 'to do/make' as a masculine singular participle — 'doing/making'.
דברים: H1697 'things/words/deeds' in plural.
חזקים: No candidates listed. Consonants match H2389 (חזק) 'strong/mighty' in masculine plural.
בזרועו: No candidates listed. Consonants match ב + זרוע (H2220 'arm') + ו (3ms suffix) = 'with his arm'.
הגאים: No candidates listed. Consonants match ה + גאה/גא (H1343 גֵּאֶה 'proud/haughty') in plural with article = 'the proud ones'.
במחשבת: No candidates listed. Consonants match ב + מחשבת (H4284 'thought/device/plan') in construct = 'in the thought/scheming of'.

לבו: No candidates listed but the consonants suggest an anomalous form. Expected for 'their heart' would be לבם. However, לבו (H3820 לב 'heart' + ו 3ms suffix) could be 'his heart' referring collectively to each proud person, or the ו suffix may be used loosely for the plural referent.

verses.literal: For he [is] doing things strong with his arm and he [is] despising the proud in [the] thought of their heart

verses.translation: And he brings down [humbles] the mighty and the lofty from their thrones [seats of power], and lifts up the lowly [humble, downtrodden]

translation_notes: והוא: H1931 with conjunction, 'and he'.
textual_notes: משפיל: No candidates listed. Consonants match H8213 (שפל) 'to be low/humble' in Hiphil participle = 'one who brings low/humbles'.
החזקים: H2389 'strong/mighty' with article, masculine plural.
והגבוהים: No candidates listed. Consonants match ו + ה + גבוה (H1364 'high, lofty, exalted') in masculine plural = 'and the exalted/lofty ones'.

מאריותם: No candidates listed. This is a difficult form. The consonants suggest מ (from) + אריות + ם (3mp suffix). The most likely root is related to a word for 'throne/seat' — possibly a variant or late Hebrew form. The Aramaic/late Hebrew כורסיא or the Hebrew כסא would be expected for 'throne', but אריות from ארי (H738 'lion') would give 'from their lions' which is incoherent. Another possibility: if this is a scribal rendering of a word for 'seats/places of honor', it may be an unusual form. Given the context of deposing the mighty, 'from their thrones/seats' is the contextually demanded meaning, though the exact etymology is uncertain.
ומגביה: No candidates listed. Consonants match ו + מגביה from גבה (H1361 'to be high') in Hiphil participle = 'and one who raises up/lifts high'.

ה(פלים: The ( indicates a damaged/uncertain letter. In context of being contrasted with 'the strong and exalted', the lowly/humble is expected. Consonants likely reconstruct as השפלים from שפל (H8217 'low, humble') = 'the lowly ones'. The missing letter is likely שׁ, giving השפלים.

verses.literal: And he [is] bringing-low the strong and the exalted from their thrones and raising-up the lowly

verses.translation: The hungry he fills [satisfies] with every good thing, and sends away the wealthy empty [empty-handed, with nothing]

translation_notes: ממלא: Candidates: H4390 'to fill', H4391 'to fill (Aramaic)', H4392 'full', H4393 'fullness', H4394 'consecration', H3808 'not'. As a participle with prefix מ describing God's action toward the hungry, H4390 'filling' is the clear reading.
כל: H3605 'all/every' as quantifier before טוב.

טוב: Candidates: H2895 'to be good', H2896 'good (adj/noun)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness/the best'. As a noun following כל, H2896 'good' or H2898 'goodness' both work; H2896 as the broader adjective/noun 'good things' fits naturally.
textual_notes: הרעבים: No candidates listed. Consonants match ה + רעב (H7457 רָעֵב 'hungry') in masculine plural = 'the hungry ones'.
ועוזב: No candidates listed. Consonants match ו + עוזב from עזב (H5800 'to leave, forsake, abandon') as participle = 'and forsaking/leaving/sending away'.
העשירים: No candidates listed. Consonants match ה + עשיר (H6223 'rich, wealthy') in masculine plural = 'the rich/wealthy ones'.
רקים: No candidates listed. Consonants match H7386 (רֵק/רֵיק 'empty, vain') in masculine plural = 'empty/empty-handed'.
The apostrophe at the end likely marks a section break or paragraph marker in the manuscript.

verses.literal: The hungry [he] fills [with] all good and [he] forsakes the rich empty

verses.translation: He redeems [rescues, ransoms] Israel his servant-son [his child], remembering his steadfast lovingkindnesses [covenant mercies]

translation_notes: ישראל: H3478 'Israel' as the object of redemption.
textual_notes: פודה: No candidates listed. Consonants match H6299 (פדה) 'to ransom, redeem' as a masculine singular participle = 'redeeming/one who redeems'.

בנו: No candidates listed. Consonants match H1121 (בן) 'son/child' with 3ms suffix = 'his son'. Could alternatively be parsed as H1129 (בנה) 'to build' with 3ms suffix, but 'his son' referring to Israel as God's child is the contextually coherent reading.
זוכר: No candidates listed. Consonants match H2142 (זכר) 'to remember' as a masculine singular participle = 'remembering'.

מחסדיו: No candidates listed. Consonants match מ (from/of) + חסד (H2617 'kindness/lovingkindness') in plural with 3ms suffix = 'from/of his kindnesses/mercies'. The מ prefix could indicate 'from/out of his mercies' (source/motivation) or be partitive.

verses.literal: Redeeming Israel his son remembering from his kindnesses

verses.translation: Just as he promised [vowed] to our ancestors, to Abraham and to his seed [descendants] for all ages [forever]

translation_notes: כמו: H3644 'as, thus, so' — comparative particle introducing the comparison with past promises.
שנדר: Candidates: H5087 'to promise/vow (to God)', H5088 'a promise/vow'. With ש as relative particle and the verbal form, H5087 'that he vowed/promised' fits as a verb: 'as that he promised'.
textual_notes: לאבותינו: No candidates listed. Consonants match ל + אבות (H1 אָב 'father' in feminine plural construct form, used for 'fathers/ancestors') + ינו (1cp suffix) = 'to our fathers/ancestors'.
ולזרעו: No candidates listed. Consonants match ו + ל + זרע (H2233 'seed, offspring, descendants') + ו (3ms suffix) = 'and to his seed/descendants'.

לעולמים: No candidates listed. Consonants match ל + עולם (H5769 'long duration, antiquity, futurity, forever') with ים suffix functioning as intensifier = 'for ages, forever, in perpetuity'. The ים here amplifies the sense of eternity rather than indicating a numerical plural.

verses.literal: As that he vowed to our fathers to Abraham and to his seed to ages

verses.translation: And Miriam [or: Mary] took up her dwelling with Elisheba [Elizabeth] for close to three months, and afterward she returned to her home [which was] in the sanctuary [holy place, temple]

translation_notes: עמדה (consonants עמד+ה): H5979 'a station, domicile' — she stationed/settled herself. This fits the context of a prolonged stay with Elisheba.
עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with (preposition)'. Chose H5973 because the preposition 'with' fits — she dwelt with Elisheba.

כמעט (כ+מעט): Candidates: H4591 'to lessen', H4592 'a little/few', H4593 'sharp', H5842 'stylus'. The כ prefix + H4592 yields 'nearly/almost', which fits naturally before a number — nearly three months.

שלשה: Candidates: H8030 'Shilshah (name)', H8031 'Shalishah (place)', H7716 'sheep'. None match 'three' directly in Strong's, but שלשה is the standard Hebrew word for 'three' (feminine form). The consonants ש-ל-ש-ה clearly spell the numeral three, which fits before 'months'.

שבה (consonants שבה): H7617 'to transport into captivity' — however the consonants ש-ב-ה also support the root שוב 'to return' (H7725) in a 3fs perfect form. In context, 'she returned' is the only coherent reading. The captivity meaning produces a bizarre image.
במקדש: Candidates: H4720 'sanctuary/consecrated place', H6944 'sacred place'. Chose H4720 — she returned to her house which was in/at the sanctuary.
textual_notes: חףדשים appears to be חדשים (months) with an anomalous ף — possibly a scribal error or variant spelling. Read as חדשים 'months'.
בביתה lacks a Strong's candidate entry — it is בבית+ה 'to/in her house', standard Hebrew prepositional construction.
שבה could theoretically be H7617 'captivity' but in context must be from שוב 'to return' (H7725), which was not provided as a candidate. The consonants support both roots.

The final phrase 'to her house in the sanctuary' is ambiguous: does it mean her house was located at/in the sanctuary complex, or that she returned first to her house and then to the sanctuary? The Hebrew בביתה במקדש most naturally reads as her home being in/at the sanctuary.

verses.literal: And Miriam stationed herself with Elisheba nearly three months and after she returned to her house in the sanctuary

translation_notes: והיה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist, be, become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 — 'and there was/came to be' fits the narrative progression: she gave birth and there was for her a son.
בן: Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'a son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 — the context clearly calls for the common noun 'son'.
ללדת: The root ילד 'to bear/give birth' with ל prefix (infinitive construct) — 'to give birth'. The candidate listing shows דת 'edict' but the full consonantal form ללדת is clearly ל+לדת from ילד.
textual_notes: ותלד has no Strong's candidate listed but is clearly ו+תלד, wayyiqtol 3fs of ילד 'to give birth'.

verses.literal: Elisheba there [was] for her to give birth and she gave birth and there was for her a son

verses.translation: And [her] neighbors and her relatives heard of that exalted loving-kindness [grace, covenant-faithfulness] of hers, and they rejoiced with her together [as one]

translation_notes: עמה: Candidates: H5980 'conjunction, near, beside, with', H5981 'Ummah (place)'. Chose H5980 — 'with her' fits perfectly in the clause 'they rejoiced with her together'.
יחד: Candidates: H3161 'to be/become one', H3162 'unitedly, together (adverb)'. Chose H3162 — the adverb 'together' modifies 'they rejoiced with her', producing a natural image.
ה<כנים: The < appears to be a textual corruption or uncertain letter. The context (neighbors hearing news) suggests השכנים 'the neighbors' — from שכן 'neighbor/dwelling'.
]חסדיה: The ] bracket indicates textual damage. Reading חסדיה 'her loving-kindness/grace' from חסד (H2617).
המעולה: From root עלה, meaning 'the exalted/supreme' — describes the greatness of the חסד shown to her.
textual_notes: ה<כנים has a damaged/uncertain character marked by <. Most likely השכנים 'the neighbors' based on context.
]חסדיה has a bracket indicating textual damage at the beginning. Reading as חסדיה 'her loving-kindness'.
מאותה could be parsed as מ+אותה 'from/of that [feminine]' — a demonstrative construction pointing to the exalted grace.

verses.literal: And heard the neighbors and her relatives of that supreme [kindness/grace] of hers and they rejoiced with her together

words: in order that / on account of

translation_notes: בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of, in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 — 'in order that they would circumcise' makes perfect narrative sense.
הבן: Candidates: H1894 'ebony', H1121 'son'. Chose H1121 with the definite article ה — 'the son'. Circumcising ebony is absurd.
שם: Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name/appellation', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name (Aramaic)'. Chose H8034 — 'they called him [the] name of his father' is the coherent reading.
ונאספו[: The bracket suggests textual damage. Reading as ונאספו from root אסף 'to gather' — 'and they gathered'.
שימולו: Reading as ש+ימולו — 'that they would circumcise', from מול 'to circumcise' (H4135). The ש prefix functions as the relative/purpose particle.
textual_notes: ונאספו[ has a bracket indicating possible textual damage at the end.
בשמונת הימים literally reads 'in the eight of the days' — an unusual construction for 'on the eighth day', but the meaning is clear from context.

verses.literal: They heard and they gathered in the eight of the days in order that they would circumcise the son and they called to him [the] name of his father Zechariah

verses.translation: And his mother answered and said, No, it shall not be so — rather [but], his name shall be Yochanan [John, meaning: YHWH is gracious]

translation_notes: כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/right', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 — 'it will not be so' is the natural reading in a naming dispute.

אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay, truly, yet (adversative)'. Chose H61 — 'but/rather' serves as the adversative conjunction needed here: 'not so, but rather his name shall be Yochanan'.
ואמרה: H565 'something said' — but here functioning as the verb 'and she said', from root אמר.
textual_notes: וענתה lacks a listed candidate — clearly from root ענה 'to answer' (H6030) in 3fs wayyiqtol form with 3fs suffix or simply feminine ending.
