verses.literal: And answered his mother and said no it will be so but that his name will be Yochanan

verses.translation: And they said to her, There is no [one] fitting [or: worthy] in your family that would have such a name [as this]

translation_notes: אין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 — 'there is not' introduces the objection: no one in your family has such a name.
כזה: כ+זה. Candidates for זה: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'like this' (כ = 'like' + זה = 'this'), meaning 'such as this name'.
textual_notes: ראוי lacks a Strong's candidate — it appears to be a later Hebrew/Rabbinic form meaning 'fitting, worthy, proper' (from root ראה 'to see/regard').
ה ם appear as separated fragments — likely השם 'the name' with textual damage or spacing issue. The ש is missing or illegible between ה and ם.
במשפחתך is ב+משפחת+ך 'in your family/clan' from משפחה (H4940).

verses.literal: And they said to her there is not fitting in your family that there would be for you like this the name

verses.translation: And they made a sign [gesture] to his father [asking] how he desired [wished, was pleased] his name would be

translation_notes: ועשו: The candidate listed is H6215 'Esau', but the consonants ו+עשו clearly parse as waw-consecutive + 3mp perfect of עשה 'to do/make' (H6213). Choosing 'they made' because the context demands a verb — they made a sign to his father. 'Esau' as a proper noun here is nonsensical.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 — 'he' as the subject pronoun: 'how he desires'.

חפץ: Candidates: H2654 'to incline, be pleased, desire', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire'. Chose H2654 as the verb — 'he desires/wishes [that] his name would be'. This produces the natural question: how does the father want the child named?
textual_notes: סימן has no Strong's entry provided — it is a post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew word meaning 'sign, signal, gesture'.
The apostrophe ' at the end may indicate a textual break, lacuna, or section marker.
ועשו consonants match both עשה 'to make' (3mp) and עשו 'Esau' — context decisively favors the verb.

verses.literal: And they made a sign to his father how he desires it would be his name

verses.translation: And Zechariah asked for a single tablet [writing board], on which he wrote: 'Yochanan — that is his name.' And all who were there were greatly astonished [amazed] at this

translation_notes: שאל: Candidates: H7592 'to inquire/request/demand', H7593 'to inquire (Aramaic)', H7594 'Sheal (name)'. Chose H7592 — 'he requested/asked for' a tablet. The narrative context is that he is mute and needs a writing surface.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 — 'one tablet' / 'a single tablet'.
אשר (first): Candidates include H834 'who/which/that' and others. Chose H834 — relative pronoun 'which' introducing 'on which he wrote'.

כתב: Candidates: H3789 'to write/inscribe', H3790 'to write (Aramaic)', H3791 'a writing', H3792 'a writing (Aramaic)'. Chose H3789 — the verb 'he wrote', fitting the action of inscribing on the tablet.
שם (second occurrence): Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name'. Chose H8033 — 'all who were there' is the natural adverbial use, distinct from שמו 'his name' which appears earlier.

מזה: Candidates: H4198 'exhausted', H4199 'Mizzah (name)', H2088 'this/that'. Chose מ+זה = 'from this / at this' (preposition מן + demonstrative H2088). They were astonished at this — a coherent concluding image.
אשר (second): Same analysis — H834 'who/that', connecting 'all who were there'.
textual_notes: תמהו has no Strong's candidate listed — it is from root תמה 'to be astonished/amazed' (H8539) in 3mp perfect.
הוא שמו could be read as a nominal clause 'he is his name' (i.e., 'that is his name') or as an emphatic identification. Both yield essentially the same meaning.

verses.literal: And Zechariah asked [for] a tablet one which on it he wrote Yochanan he [is] his name and all who were there were astonished greatly from this

verses.translation: And immediately the mouth of the father was opened, and his tongue spoke [again], and he blessed [praised] YHWH
words: and immediately / and from the hand

translation_notes: ומיד: The candidate is H3027 'hand'. ומיד = 'and from [the] hand', idiomatically meaning 'immediately/at once'. This is standard Hebrew usage.
האב: Candidates: H1 'father', H2 'father (Aramaic)', H3 'green plant', H4 'green plant (Aramaic)'. Chose H1 — 'the father'. The narrative is about Zechariah the father whose mouth is opened.

דברה: Candidates: H1700 'a reason/suit/manner', H1701 same, H1702 'a raft', H1703 'a word'. The consonants also support the verb דבר 'to speak' (H1696) in 3fs perfect — 'his tongue spoke'. Chose this verbal reading because 'his tongue spoke' produces a coherent image of speech being restored. The listed noun candidates don't fit syntactically.

ובירך: The candidate listed is H3409 'thigh'. However ו+בירך clearly parses as waw + piel perfect 3ms of ברך 'to bless' (H1288). The ב is part of the root, not a preposition. 'And he blessed YHWH' is the only coherent reading.
textual_notes: נפתח has no listed candidate — from root פתח 'to open' (H6605) in niphal perfect 3ms, 'was opened'.
פי has no listed candidate — construct form of פה 'mouth' (H6310).
ולשונו has no listed candidate — ו+לשון+ו 'and his tongue' from לשון (H3956).
ובירך: The only listed candidate is H3409 'thigh' (ירך), but the word must be parsed as ברך 'to bless' in piel, which was not provided as a candidate.

verses.literal: And immediately [the] mouth of the father was opened and his tongue spoke and he blessed YHWH

verses.translation: And fear [awe, dread] came upon all their neighbors, and throughout all the hill country of Judah these words [matters] were spread [reported]
words: and there was / and it came to be
the mountains of / the hill country of

translation_notes: והיה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/become/come to pass', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 — 'and there was/came to be' introduces the resulting state of fear.
פחד: Candidates: H6342 'to be startled/fear', H6343 'alarm/fear (noun)', H6344 'testicle'. Chose H6343 — the noun 'fear/dread', which serves as the subject: 'there was fear upon all their neighbors'.
בכל (both): H3605 'the whole/all' — 'in all' or 'upon all'. Standard usage.

הרי: The candidate listed is H7377 'irrigation/shower' for רי, but הרי is clearly the construct plural of הר 'mountain' (H2022) — 'the mountains/hills of'. 'The hill country of Judah' is a well-known geographic designation and produces a coherent image.

אלה: Candidates: H421 'bewail', H422 'adjure', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. However, the consonants אלה also represent the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (H428). In context, 'these words/matters' is the only reading that makes sense — it serves as the demonstrative modifying הדברים.
textual_notes: נתפ טו appears to be a single word split by textual damage — likely נתפרסמו or נתפשטו 'were spread/published'. The exact root is uncertain due to the break. The context demands a verb meaning 'were spread/reported/published'.
שכיניהם has no listed candidate — from שכן 'neighbor' (H7934) with 3mp possessive suffix: 'their neighbors'.
הדברים has no listed candidate — from דבר (H1697) 'word/matter/thing' with definite article and masculine plural: 'the words/matters'.

אלה is identified as the demonstrative 'these' (H428), though this entry was not among the provided candidates. The candidates listed all point to other roots, but the consonants אלה unambiguously also spell the common demonstrative pronoun.

verses.literal: And there was fear in all their neighbors and in all [the] mountains of Judah were spread these the words

verses.translation: And all who heard [these things] stored them away in their hearts, and said, 'What then will this child become?' For the hand [or: power] of YHWH was upon him.

translation_notes: אשר (H834 vs H833/H835/H836/H837/H838): Candidates: H834 'who/which/that', H833 'to be straight', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because this is a relative pronoun introducing 'all who heard' — the standard relative clause construction.

אי (H335 vs H336/H337/H338/H339): Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 because it forms an interrogative phrase 'what will this be?' — a question about the child's destiny.

זה first occurrence (H2088 vs H2089/H2090): H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 as the demonstrative pronoun; 'a sheep' makes no sense in an interrogative about a child's future.

הנער (H5288 vs H5286/H5287/H5289/H5290): H5288 'boy/child', H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble', H5289 'wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 with the article ה — 'the boy/child' fits perfectly as the subject of the question about the child's destiny.
שמוהו: Parsed as שמ + והו — root שים (H7760, to put/place) with 3mp suffix + 3ms object suffix. They placed them (the things heard) regarding him, i.e., stored these things in their hearts.
textual_notes: אי זה could be parsed as a single interrogative phrase 'what sort' or as two separate words 'where/what' + 'this'. The combination אי זה functions idiomatically as 'what kind of' or 'what'.
שמוהו is morphologically complex — it could theoretically be from שם (H8034 'name') as a denominative, but the context of placing things in the heart strongly supports שים (H7760 'to put/place').

verses.literal: And all who heard placed-them in their heart and said what will be this the-boy for [the] hand of YHWH was on him

verses.translation: And Zechariah his father was filled [with the] spirit of holiness [or: the holy spirit], and he prophesied and said:

translation_notes: היה (H1961 vs H1962): H1961 'to be/become', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 — 'was full' is coherent; 'ruin full of spirit' is nonsensical.

מלא (H4390/H4391/H4392/H4393/H4394 vs H3808/H3809): The consonants מלא clearly support the root meaning 'full/filled'. H4392 (adjective 'full') fits best with היה — 'was full'. The alternative reading מ + לא ('from not') is contextually absurd.

רוח (H7304/H7305/H7306/H7307/H7308): H7307 'spirit/wind/breath' is the noun reading that fits with 'full of spirit'. The verbal readings (H7304 'breathe freely', H7306 'to smell') don't fit the adjectival construction.

הקדש (H6942/H6943/H6944/H6945/H6946): H6944 'a sacred thing/sanctity' with the article — 'the holiness'. This forms the construct 'spirit of the holiness'. H6943 'Kedesh' (place) and H6946 'Kadesh' (place) don't fit; H6945 'cult prostitute' is contextually impossible.
ואמר (H559 vs H560-H564): H559 'to say' is the obvious choice in this narrative context. H563 'a lamb' and H564 'Immer' (proper noun) don't fit.
textual_notes: וניבא: No candidates were provided. Parsed as ו + נבא (root נבא, H5012, 'to prophesy') in a reflexive/passive stem. This is the standard form for 'and he prophesied'.

verses.literal: And Zechariah his-father was full [of] spirit the-holy and prophesied and said

verses.translation: Blessed be [the] Lord, [the] God of Israel, for he has visited [or: attended to] and accomplished redemption [or: ransom] for his people.

translation_notes: ברוך: The only candidate listed is H1263 (Baruk, proper name). However, the consonants ברוך are the passive participle of ברך (H1288 'to bless'), yielding 'blessed'. In a doxological opening ('Blessed be the Lord...') this is clearly the passive participle, not the proper name. I assign the gloss 'blessed' from the root ברך.
אדון (H113 vs H114): H113 'sovereign/lord' vs H114 'Addon' (proper name). Chose H113 — 'Lord God of Israel' is a standard divine epithet.
כי (H3588 vs H3587): H3588 'for/because' vs H3587 'brand/scar'. Chose H3588 — conjunction introducing the reason for blessing.
הוא (H1931 vs H1932/H1933/H1934): H1931 'he' (pronoun) fits as subject of 'visited'. The other candidates are Aramaic or verbal forms less suited here.
ישראל (H3478 vs H3479): Both refer to Israel. H3478 is the standard Hebrew form.
textual_notes: א3להי: The consonants appear to contain a textual marker or corruption (the '3'). Read as אלהי — construct form of אלהים (H430), 'God of'. The numeral in the manuscript may indicate a scribal note or variant.
פדיון: No candidates were provided. Parsed as from root פדה (H6299 'to ransom'), noun form פדיון (H6306 'ransom/redemption').
עמו: Could be עם + ו (H5971 'his people') or the preposition עם + ו (H5973 'with him'). Context strongly favors 'his people' — he made redemption for 'his people'.

verses.literal: Blessed will-be [the] Lord God-of Israel for he visited and made redemption [for] his-people

verses.translation: And he directed [or: made straight the way for] us and swiftly gave [or: hastened to grant] deliverance [or: peace, wholeness] from [the] house of David his servant.

translation_notes: ומהר (H4116 vs H4117/H4118/H4119 vs H2022/H2023): H4116 'to hurry/hasten', H4117 'to bargain for a wife', H4118 'in a hurry', H4119 'bride-price', H2022 'mountain'. Chose H4116 — 'hastened to give' is contextually coherent in a narrative about God's swift redemption. 'Mountain of giving' or 'bride-price of giving' are forced.
שלום (H7965 vs H7966/H7967): H7965 'peace/welfare/wholeness', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum' (name). Chose H7965 — deliverance/peace fits the theme of salvation from the house of David.
בית (H1004 vs H1005/H1006): H1004 'house/household/dynasty'. Chose H1004 — 'house of David' is the dynastic reference.
דוד (H1730 vs H1731/H1732): H1732 'David' (proper name), H1730 'beloved/uncle', H1731 'pot/basket'. Chose H1732 — 'house of David' is a well-known dynastic designation.
textual_notes: והיישיר: No candidates provided. Parsed as hiphil (causative) of ישר (H3474 'to be straight'), meaning 'he made straight/directed'. The ו prefix is conjunctive, and the יי may reflect a double-yod spelling of the hiphil.
תת: No candidates provided. Parsed as the infinitive construct of נתן (H5414 'to give').

נערו: Could be from נער (H5288 'boy/servant') with 3ms suffix — 'his servant/boy', or from נער (H5287 'to shake off') as a verb. Context of the house of David suggests 'his servant' — referring to David as God's servant.
The apostrophe ' between שלום and בית may represent a divine name abbreviation or a textual separator. Its exact function is unclear.
בית דוד נערו could also be read as 'the house of David his youth' (from H5290 נער 'boyhood'), but 'his servant' fits better with David as YHWH's servant.

verses.literal: And he-made-straight us and hastened to-give peace [in/from the] house-of David his-servant

verses.translation: Just as he declared through [or: from] the mouth of his holy ones, the prophets, who [have spoken] from the beginning of the age [or: from of old, from time immemorial].

translation_notes: כאשר: The כ prefix + אשר. H834 'who/which/that/as' — with כ prefix yields 'as/just as'. The other candidates (H833 'to be straight', H835 'happiness', etc.) don't form meaningful prepositional compounds here.

הגיד: The listed candidate H1517 (גיד 'tendon/thong') doesn't fit. The consonants הגיד match the hiphil perfect of נגד (H5046 'to tell/declare'). The ה prefix is the hiphil marker, not the article. 'He declared' fits the context of prophetic proclamation.

שהם (H7718 'beryl' vs H1992 'they'): The consonants ש + הם. ש functions as the relative particle (= אשר) + הם (H1992 'they'). Reading 'who they [are]' — i.e., 'who are from the beginning of the age'. H7718 'beryl/gem' produces nonsense in this context.
textual_notes: הגיד: The provided candidate (H1517 'tendon') doesn't match the context. I identify this as hiphil of נגד (H5046), which shares the consonants גד in the root but produces הגיד in the hiphil. This is the standard form for 'he declared/told'.
שהם could theoretically be the relative ש + הם ('who they are') or the gemstone שהם (H7718). Context decisively favors the relative construction.

verses.literal: As-which he-told from-[the]-mouth-of his-holy-ones the-prophets who [are] from-[the]-beginning-of the-age

verses.translation: Deliverance [or: peace, salvation] for us from those who hate us, and from the hand [or: power, grip] of all those who provoked us [or: stirred us to wrath].

translation_notes: שלום (H7965 vs H7966/H7967): H7965 'peace/welfare/safety' fits as the object of deliverance — salvation from enemies. H7966 'requital' is possible but less natural. H7967 'Shallum' (name) doesn't fit.
ומיד: ו + מ + יד. H3027 'hand' vs H3028 (Aramaic 'hand'). Chose H3027 — 'from the hand of' meaning 'from the power/grip of'.
כל (H3605 vs H3606): H3605 Hebrew 'all' vs H3606 Aramaic 'all'. Chose H3605 for Hebrew context.
textual_notes: משונאינו: No candidates provided. Parsed as מ + שונאינו — from the root שנא (H8130 'to hate'), participle with 1cp suffix: 'from those hating us / from our enemies'.

אותן: No candidates provided. This appears to be a demonstrative/pronoun 'those' (possibly related to את sign of the accusative, or אותו with plural ending). It functions as 'those' referring to the people described in the following relative clause.

שהקציפונו: No candidates provided. Parsed as ש (relative) + הקציפו (hiphil of קצף H7107 'to be wrathful', causative: 'provoked to anger') + נו (1cp suffix 'us'). 'Who provoked us to anger' or 'who enraged us'.

verses.literal: Peace to-us from-those-hating-us and-from-[the]-hand-of all those who-provoked-us-to-anger

verses.translation: To show [or: do, perform] faithful love [or: kindness, covenant loyalty] with our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant [or: the holiness of his charge/command].

translation_notes: לעשות: The candidates H6219 'shining/polished' and H6220 'Ashvath' (name) don't fit. The consonants עשות are the infinitive construct of עשה (H6213 'to do/make') with ל prefix. 'To do kindness' is a standard Hebrew expression.
חסד (H2616 vs H2617 vs H2618): H2617 'kindness/covenant loyalty' (noun) fits as the object of 'to do'. H2616 (verb 'to be kind') would need different syntax. H2618 'Chesed' (name) doesn't fit.
עם (H5971 vs H5973): H5973 'with' (preposition) vs H5971 'people'. 'To do kindness with our fathers' uses the preposition. 'To do kindness [the] people of our fathers' is awkward.

ולזכור: The candidate H2138 'male' and H2139 'Zakkur' don't fit. The consonants זכור are the infinitive construct of זכר (H2142 'to remember') with ל + ו prefix. 'And to remember' fits the context of recalling the covenant.
textual_notes: קדו<ת: Contains a textual corruption or scribal mark (<). Read as קדושת — construct form of קדושה (from H6944 'holiness'). 'The holiness of his command' or 'his holy [covenant]'.

צואתו: No candidates provided. Parsed as צוא/צוה + תו. Most likely from צוה (H6680 'to command'), noun form צואה (H6673 'command/charge') with 3ms suffix: 'his command/charge'. Alternatively could relate to H6675 צואה 'filth/excrement', but this is contextually impossible in a passage about God's holy covenant.

verses.literal: To-do kindness with our-fathers and-to-remember [the] holiness-of his-command

verses.translation: And the oath that he swore to Abraham our father — [it] will be granted [or: fulfilled, given] to us.

translation_notes: לאברהם (H85): Only one candidate — Abraham, the patriarch. Fits perfectly in context of the oath sworn to the ancestor.
textual_notes: וה<בועה: Contains a textual corruption or scribal mark (<). Read as והשבועה — from שבועה (H7621 'oath') with the article and conjunctive ו. 'And the oath'.
שנשבע: No candidates provided. Parsed as ש (relative 'that') + נשבע (niphal of שבע H7650 'to swear'): 'that he swore'.

נתון: No candidates provided. Parsed as the passive participle (qal passive / infinitive absolute) of נתן (H5414 'to give'): 'given/granted'. With יהיה this forms a periphrastic construction: 'will be given'.

verses.literal: And-the-oath that he-swore to-Abraham our-father will-be given to-us

verses.translation: So that he would rescue us from our enemies, [and] without fear [or: dread] we would serve [or: worship] him.

translation_notes: בעבור (H5668 vs H5669): H5668 'on account of / in order that' vs H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 — purpose clause 'in order that he deliver us' fits the context of divine rescue.

פחד (H6342 vs H6343 vs H6344): H6343 'fear/dread' (noun) vs H6342 'to fear' (verb) vs H6344 'testicle'. Chose H6343 — the noun 'without fear' following בלי. The verb form would require different syntax, and H6344 is contextually absurd.
textual_notes: שיצילנו: No candidates provided. Parsed as ש (relative/purpose) + יציל (hiphil imperfect of נצל H5337 'to deliver/rescue') + נו (1cp suffix 'us'): 'that he will deliver us'.
מאויבינו: No candidates provided. Parsed as מ + אויבינו — from אויב (H341 'enemy') with 1cp suffix: 'from our enemies'.
נעבוד: No candidates provided. Parsed as 1cp imperfect of עבד (H5647 'to serve/worship'): 'we will serve'.

verses.literal: In-order-that he-will-deliver-us from-our-enemies without fear we-will-serve him

verses.translation: In holiness [or: consecration] and in purity [or: cleanness] before him all our days.

translation_notes: כל (H3605 vs H3606): H3605 Hebrew 'all' vs H3606 Aramaic 'all'. Chose H3605 for Hebrew context.
textual_notes: בקדו<ה: Contains a textual corruption or scribal mark (<). Read as בקדושה — 'in holiness', from the root קדש (H6944).
ובטהףרה: Contains a textual corruption or scribal mark (ף). Read as ובטהרה — 'and in purity', from the root טהר (H2893 'purification/purity').

ימינו could be parsed as ימי + נו ('our days', from יום H3117) or as ימין + ו ('his right hand', from ימין H3225). The context of 'all our days' — describing the duration of service — strongly favors 'our days'. Singular 'his right hand' doesn't fit with כל in this context.

verses.literal: In-holiness and-in-purity before-him all our-days

verses.translation: And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High [or: supremely exalted], for you will walk before the Lord [the Sovereign One] in order to prepare the ways so that they will be directed [toward] wholeness [or: peace, well-being] — you will fulfill his service, and [bring] peace in the way of peace and in the way of God [the Mighty One]

translation_notes: ואתה (אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'thou/you'. Chose H859 because the sentence addresses someone directly ('and you, child'), fitting a second-person address.

נער: Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'boy/child', H5289 'wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the text addresses a young person who will be called a prophet — 'child' fits naturally as a vocative.
נביא: Candidates: H5029 'a prophet', H5030 'a prophet/inspired man'. Chose H5030 as the more common biblical term for prophet.

]מהמאד[: This word appears bracketed/damaged in the manuscript. The consonants suggest מן + המאד, 'of the most/exceedingly'. Read as 'of the Most [High]' connecting to נעלה (exalted) — together: 'prophet of the Most High Exalted.'
שלום (first): Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum'. Chose H7965 because the passage concerns directing paths toward peace/wholeness.

האל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these/those', H413 'near/to'. Chose H410 because with the article ה it reads 'the God/the Mighty One', completing 'in the way of God' as a parallel to 'in the way of peace.'
textual_notes: The bracketed word ]מהמאד[ appears to be a scribal correction or damaged text. The consonants suggest 'of the most' but the exact reading is uncertain. It may be a compound: מן + המאד (from/of the exceedingly) modifying נעלה (exalted), yielding 'prophet of the Most High/Exalted.'
מיו<רים contains a damaged character (<). The likely reading is מיושרים from ישר (to be straight/directed), meaning 'straightened/directed,' but this is uncertain.
תשלום could be parsed as 'you will complete/fulfill' (from שלם, to be complete) or as a noun 'recompense/completion.' The verbal reading fits better with the preceding clauses of purpose.

The final clauses 'שלום תשלום עבדו ושלום בדרך שלום ובדרך האל' have ambiguous phrase boundaries. It could read: 'peace you-will-complete his-service, and-peace in-way-of peace and-in-way-of God' or alternatively segment differently.

verses.literal: And you child will be called a prophet of the Most High exalted for you will walk before the Lord in order that you will prepare the ways that will be directed [toward] peace you will complete his service and peace in [the] way [of] peace and in [the] way of God

verses.translation: And to give complete [or: full, whole] healing to his people for the forgiveness [or: pardon] of their iniquities [or: sins, transgressions]

textual_notes: רפואה (healing/remedy) is not in the provided Strong's candidates but is a standard Hebrew noun from רפא (H7495, to heal). The form is clear from context.
שלימה (complete/whole) derives from שלם and means 'complete, whole, perfect.' It modifies רפואה — 'complete healing.'
למחילת (for the forgiveness of) derives from מחילה (forgiveness/pardon), a post-biblical Hebrew form. No Strong's number is standard for this noun, though the root מחל relates to pardoning.
עונותיהם (their iniquities) is the plural of עון (H5771) with third-person masculine plural suffix.

verses.literal: And to give healing complete to his people for [the] forgiveness of their iniquities

verses.translation: On account of his mercies [or: lovingkindnesses] by which he visits [or: attends to] us — he who is [from on] high [or: the exalted one]

translation_notes: בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because the context speaks of a reason (his mercies) for the visitation.

שבהן: The ש is a relative particle ('that/which'), ב is 'in', הן is the pronoun 'them' (H2004). Together: 'in which' or 'by which.' The candidates H931 'thumb' and H932 'Bohan' are irrelevant here — the ב+הן parsing as preposition + pronoun makes clear contextual sense referring back to חסדיו (his mercies).
שהוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as the pronoun 'he [is]' in a relative clause 'who he [is]' — describing the one from on high.
מרום: Candidates: H4791 'altitude/elevated place', H4792 'Merom (lake)'. Chose H4791 because the text describes a divine figure visiting from on high, not a geographic location.
textual_notes: חסד]יו[ has a partially damaged/bracketed suffix. The likely reading is חסדיו 'his mercies/lovingkindnesses' (חסד H2617 with 3ms suffix), but the brackets indicate manuscript uncertainty.
מי שהוא מרום could be read as 'he who is [from] on high' (identifying a divine visitor) or 'whoever is exalted' (a more generic statement). The former fits the context of a divine visitation.

verses.literal: On account of his mercies in which he visits us [the] one who is [on] high

verses.translation: And he shone light upon [or: illuminated] those who are dwelling in deep darkness [or: thick gloom] and in [the] shadow of death, in order that our feet will be guided into light on the way [or: path] of peace [or: wholeness, well-being]

translation_notes: ובצלמות: H6757 'shade of death/the grave/calamity.' This is the only candidate and fits perfectly with the parallel בערפליות (in thick darkness).
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 — purpose clause: 'in order that our feet will be illuminated.'
בדרך: Candidates: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'a road/way'. Chose H1870 as the noun 'way/path' — 'in the way of peace.'
שלום: Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare', H7966 'requital', H7967 'Shallum'. Chose H7965 — 'peace' completes the image of walking in the path of wholeness.
textual_notes: מאו+רות contains a marked character (+). The likely reading is מאורות from אור (light, H216), meaning 'illuminated/given light.' The + may indicate a scribal insertion or uncertain letter.
תהיו is plural ('will be'), agreeing with רגלינו ('our feet'). This confirms the subject is the feet being guided/illuminated.

שיושבין uses the participial form with a final ן (-in), a later Hebrew/Aramaic plural ending rather than classical Hebrew ים (-im). This suggests the manuscript may reflect a later Hebrew dialect or Aramaic influence.

verses.literal: And he illuminated them who are sitting in thick darkness and in shadow of death in order that our feet will be illuminated in [the] way of peace

verses.translation: And the child was growing and becoming strong [or: strengthened] in the spirit of holiness [the Holy Spirit], and [was] dwelling in the wilderness places until the time that he revealed [or: showed] himself to Israel

translation_notes: והנער: Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'boy/child', H5289 'wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the narrative follows a child growing up — the article ה indicates a specific, previously mentioned child.
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/become', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because this is a narrative auxiliary 'was' used with participles (growing, strengthening).

גדל: Candidates: H1431 'to be/make large, grow', H1432 'large', H1433 'magnitude', H1434 'thread/tassel', H1435 'Giddel'. Chose H1431 as the verbal form 'growing' — participial use with היה for continuous past action.
וחזק: Candidates: H2388 'to be strong/strengthen', H2389 'strong', H2390 'powerful', H2391 'help', H2392 'power'. Chose H2388 as the verb 'becoming strong' parallel to גדל (growing).

ברוח: Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room', H7306 'to smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 'wind/spirit (Aramaic)'. Chose H7307 because 'spirit' paired with הקדש (holiness) yields 'spirit of holiness' — the domain in which the child was strengthened.

הקדש: Candidates: H6942 'to be clean/holy', H6943 'Kedesh', H6944 'sacred place/thing/sanctity', H6945 'devotee', H6946 'Kadesh'. Chose H6944 because with the article it reads 'the holiness' or 'the holy,' completing 'spirit of the holiness' = 'the Holy Spirit.'
עד: Candidates: H5703 'terminus/duration', H5704 'as far as/until', H5707 'witness'. Chose H5704 as the temporal preposition 'until' — 'until the time.'
שהראה: The ש is a relative particle, ה is the hiphil prefix, ראה (H7200) is 'to see.' In hiphil: 'to cause to see/show.' Chose H7200 in causative stem meaning 'he showed/revealed.'
לישראל: Candidates: H3478 'Israel', H3479 'Israel (Aramaic)'. Chose H3478 as the standard Hebrew form.
textual_notes: עומד (standing/dwelling) could imply either temporary standing or sustained residence. In context with במדברות (in the wilderness places), it likely means 'dwelling/remaining' rather than merely standing upright.
במדברות is the plural of מדבר (wilderness, H4057) with a feminine plural ending -ות, meaning 'wilderness places' or 'desert regions.' This is a less common plural form.

עצמו (himself) could theoretically derive from עצם (H6106 'bone' or H6105 'to be strong'), but in post-biblical Hebrew עצמו functions as a reflexive pronoun 'himself,' which fits the context of 'he showed himself.'

verses.literal: And the child was growing and becoming strong in [the] spirit of holiness and standing in [the] wilderness places until the time that he showed himself to Israel
